page.layout: One page of text. Top: printed ornament and page number "18". Below: heading CAPUT PRIMVM / DE MENDACIO. Then a block of two indented scripture verses (Genes. 27.6-8). Then a smaller-type summary paragraph of numbered argument references. Then the main text with a historiated initial and a block of text with two left-margin reference notes (a, b) at the bottom left. Catchword "Sed" at lower right.

main_text.head: CAPVT PRIMVM. DE MENDACIO.

p.i: Genes. 27. 6. Rebecca alloquuta est Iacobum filium suum dicendo: ecce audiui patrem tuum, loquentem cum Esauo fratre tuo, dicendo;
7. Affer mihi venationem, & para mihi cupedias quas comedam: post, benedicam tibi coram Iehoua, priusquam moriar.
8. Nunc itaque fili mi, ausculta voci meæ: rei quam ego præcipio tibi: Et quæ sequuntur.

AETERNA Dei electio, & decretum ante omnia secula, vt in singulis filiorum Adæ, locum habuit & habebit, ita in nullis illustrius & luculentius, quam in gemina Isaaci prole, Esauo & Iacob. De quibus multa sacræ pronunciarunt literæ, vt ad Romanos nono:Rom. 9. 13. {a}Iacob dilexi, Esauum vero odio habui, Malachiæ primo:Malach. 1. 2. 3. {b}Nonne frater fuit Esau Iacobo: Esauum vero odio habui: ideo di-sposui[?] montes eius desolationi, & possessionem eius draconibus deser-ti:

page.notes: The marginal references at the bottom left ("a Rom.9.13." and "b Malach. 1. 2.3.") are shown as notes beside their marks. The printed line "2. 3." is set under "Malach. 1." and is read here as "2.3.", which is uncertain. "di-sposui" is partly unclear at the line break (si/s shapes), so the reading "disposui" is marked [?]. The catchword "Sed" is at lower right and is not part of the running text. Long s is transcribed as s. The Greek/Latin spelling is kept as printed.
